ai.description: This lizard reaches 20 cm in length with a brownish body and a distinct white stripe along the flanks. It features a prominent nuchal crest and a long, slender tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Salea anamallayana* is best distinguished by its prominent, continuous crest of large, lanceolate spines running along the nape and back, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Anaimalai spiny lizard inhabits high-altitude shola forests and adjacent grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Anaimalai spiny lizard is primarily diurnal and displays a unique defensive strategy by freezing against tree bark, using its cryptic coloration to blend into the forest.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Salea anamallayana* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Anaimalai Spiny Lizard is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests and grasslands of the Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically above 1,500 meters.
